newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen well-bid in Asia, but upside limited.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen well-bid in Asia, but upside limited.

text.p: The dollar is likely to remain firm against the yen in Asia on Friday after a downside test on Thursday ended in failure, but the upside could be heavy due to fears of intervention by the Bank of Japan (BOJ), traders said.
"The dollar recovered overnight after shorts were squeezed, but there isn't yet much interest in building up fresh long dollar positions," said a Japanese city bank dealer.

He said upside resistance in the dollar could be stiff due to possible dollar sales by exporters, who may hope to arrange forward dollar sales ahead of the Golden Week holiday in Japan later this month.
Dealers said exporter dollar sales are likely to emerge around 126.20-30 yen, although stop-loss dollar buying is likely to be triggered around 126.30 yen.

"The dollar could stay well-bid in early trade since there are still short dollar positions in the market," said a dealer at a European bank in Tokyo. "But later, once those shorts are squared, the dollar may resume its easing," he added.

Dealers said the greenback was likely to find initial support at 125.70 yen and then at 125.50. The dollar fell as low as 125.08 yen on Thursday in Tokyo, but Japanese investor bids prevented it from slipping further.

A trust bank dealer said the dollar could find buying interest around 1.7230 marks despite overnight remarks by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer that pushed the dollar lower versus the mark in New York.

Tietmeyer said the mark's current level in foreign exchange markets correctly reflects economic fundamentals. He said the bank does not want a weak mark and remains interested in having a strong mark.
"His remarks had some impact on dollar/mark but did not imply any clear future direction in dollar/mark," said the trust bank dealer. --Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-1396
